prompt: Complete NameSorters: byAge() returns a Comparator ordering Person records by age ascending, and byNameLengthThenAlpha() orders by name length with alphabetical tie-breaks.
explanation: Comparator factory methods build comparators from key-extractor functions: comparingInt handles primitive int keys without boxing, and thenComparing chains a secondary ordering that only applies when the primary keys tie. Because record components generate accessor methods, method references like Person::age and Person::name slot straight in. The explicit (Person p) lambda parameter type in the length comparator helps type inference when the call is immediately chained.
hints: Comparator.comparingInt turns an int-extracting function such as an age accessor reference into a whole Comparator.
For the second comparator, extract the name length with a lambda; spelling the parameter type, e.g. (Person p) -> ..., helps inference when you chain calls.
Chain .thenComparing with a name extractor to break length ties alphabetically.
